name: Soya Chaap Masala
ingredients: 250g soya chaap (soy chunks on sticks, cut into pieces)
1 tbsp Kashmiri red chili powder (for color and mild heat)
1 tbsp dried fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi), crushed
instructions: 1. Heat mustard oil in a heavy-bottomed pan until smoking, then reduce heat. Add cumin seeds, bay leaf, cardamom, and cinnamon; sizzle for 10 seconds.
2. Add chopped onions and sauté on medium heat until deep golden brown (about 8-10 mins). Stir in ginger-garlic paste and green chilies; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
3. Pour in tomato puree, turmeric, red chili powder, and coriander powder. Cook on low heat, stirring occasionally, until the oil separates (about 5-7 mins).
4. Whisk yogurt into the masala, then add 1 cup warm water. Season with salt. Bring to a gentle simmer.
5. While the gravy simmers, pan-fry or grill the soya chaap pieces in a separate pan with a little oil until lightly charred on all sides.  (Skip this step if using pre-cooked chaap).
6. Add the soya chaap to the simmering gravy, cover, and cook on low heat for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chaap is tender and absorbs the flavors.
7. Stir in heavy cream and crushed kasuri methi. Simmer for 2 more minutes. Sprinkle garam masala and garnish with fresh cilantro. Serve hot with naan or steamed rice.
description: A robust, smoky symphony of spiced soy and earthy aromatics, wrapped in a velvety gravy that whispers of rustic Punjabi kitchens.
